$$ \min_{U}\frac{1}{2}U^{\top}H U+\Big(\Gamma^{\top}\bar{Q}\big(\Phi x_{e,k}+\Delta(\hat{d})\big)-\bar{R}U_{d}(\hat{d})\Big)^{\top}U, $$

with $U = [F_{\mathrm{mpc},0}; \ldots; F_{\mathrm{mpc},N-1}] \in \mathbb{R}^N$, $H = \Gamma^\top \bar{Q} \Gamma + \bar{R}$, $Q = \mathrm{diag}(K_d, D_d)$, and $\Phi \in \mathbb{R}^{2N \times 2}$, $\Gamma$ precomputed once (constant $A_d$). When no interaction constraint is active the solution is the closed form
$$ U^{\star}=-H^{-1}\Big\lceil\Gamma^{\top}\bar{Q}\big(\Phi x_{e}+\Delta(\hat{d})\big)-\bar{R}U_{d}(\hat{d})\Big\rceil, $$

a matrix–vector multiply. With constant  $ \Lambda_n $ over the horizon,  $ \Delta(\hat{d}) + \Gamma U_d(\hat{d}) = 0 $, so the change of variables  $ V = U - U_d $ reduces the optimizer to the nominal interaction-dynamics regulator in  $ V $. When a constraint binds, OSQP [16] solves the condensed QP reusing the cached factorization. The minimization is subject to tendon limits, curvature limits, and the contact-force interaction bound.

Force-safety interaction constraint. The corrective input  $ F_{\mathrm{mpc}} $ is the tip-normal force, and the two-layer command is realized as the tendon tension  $ T_k = -(u_{\mathrm{ff},k} + F_{\mathrm{mpc},k}) / J_n (\kappa_k) $ with the tip-space elastic feedforward  $ u_{\mathrm{ff}} = k_{\mathrm{eff}} y_d $ ( $ J_n $ bounded away from zero; Section VI-B). The predicted normal contact force—the applied tip force beyond the catheter's own elastic restoring—is then
$$ \hat{F}_{n,k}=J_{n}(\kappa_{k})\left|T_{k}\right|-k_{\mathrm{e f f}}\left|y_{k}\right|=k_{\mathrm{e f f}}e_{k}+F_{\mathrm{m p c},k}, $$

with any calibrated free-space friction bias absorbed into the disturbance estimate  $ \hat{d} $ (Remark 1). Because the compliant elastic term  $ k_{\mathrm{eff}}e_k $ is small over the workspace ( $ |k_{\mathrm{eff}}e_k| \ll F_{\mathrm{safe}} $), the hard predicted-force bound  $ |\hat{F}_n, k| \leq F_{\mathrm{safe}} $ is enforced to leading order by the box constraint on the corrective force,
$$ -F_{\mathrm{s a f e}}\leq F_{\mathrm{m p c},k}\leq F_{\mathrm{s a f e}}, $$
applied directly in the QP. This bounds the controller-induced/predicted quasi-static normal force; fast environment-induced damping spikes are handled by approach-velocity limits (Section VI-F).

Theorem 1 (LQR-impedance equivalence). In the unconstrained, disturbance-free limit (d ≡ 0, no active constraints) the receding-horizon law is the static linear state feedback  $ F_{mpc} = K_{eff} e + D_{eff} \dot{e} - \text{the LQR-realized instance of the classical catheter impedance law } u_{imp} = \hat{C} \dot{k} + \hat{K} + J_n (K_{eff} e + D_{eff} \dot{e}) $, realizing the effective tip-normal impedance  $ Z_{eff}(s, \kappa) \approx \Lambda_n(\kappa) s^2 + D_{eff} s + K_{eff} - \text{where the realized gains } (K_{eff}, D_{eff}) $ are the unconstrained LQR feedback for the weights (Q, R). The unconstrained predictive interaction controller is therefore an LQR-tuned classical impedance, with the realized gains the Riccati image of the cost weights (Remark 2); it is not a free rendering of a prescribed  $ (K_d, D_d) $ (following [13], Theorem 1).

Proof sketch: Without constraints and with  $ d \equiv 0 $ the QP minimizer is the unconstrained stationary point  $ U^* = -H^{-1}\Gamma^\top\bar{Q}\Phi_{e} $, whose first block is a static gain  $ F_{\mathrm{mpc}} = K_{\mathrm{eff}}e + D_{\mathrm{eff}}e $; with the DARE terminal cost this is the infinite-horizon LQR feedback for  $ (Q, R) $, independent of  $ N $. After Layer-1 cancellation the residual plant is  $ \ddot{e} = -\Lambda_n^{-1}(\kappa)F_{\mathrm{mpc}} + d $; multiplying by  $ \Lambda_n(\kappa) $ gives  $ \Lambda_n\ddot{e} + D_{\mathrm{eff}}\dot{e} + K_{\mathrm{eff}}e = \Lambda_n d $, the stated impedance, and adding the feedforward  $ u_{\mathrm{ff}} = \hat{C}\hat{k} + \hat{K} + J_n\Lambda_n\ddot{y}_d $ recovers  $ u_{\mathrm{imp}} $. When constraints are active or  $ d \neq 0 $, the MPC departs from this static law—precisely its advantage.

Remark 2 (Prescribed vs. realized gains). The cost weights  $ Q = \text{diag}(K_d, D_d) $,  $ R $ are design penalties; the realized impedance ( $ K_{\text{eff}} $,  $ D_{\text{eff}} $) is their LQR (Riccati) image, so in general ( $ K_{\text{eff}} $,  $ D_{\text{eff}} $)  $ \neq $ ( $ K_d $,  $ D_d $)—in particular the cheap-control limit  $ R \rightarrow 0 $ yields a plant-determined gain, not ( $ K_d $,  $ D_d $). To render a specific ( $ K_d $,  $ D_d $) exactly, prescribe the impedance gain directly ( $ F_{mpc} = K_d e + D_d e $), making the equivalence exact at the cost of the predictive look-ahead (cf. [13], Remark 2).
### IV. STABILITY ANALYSIS

Theorem 2 (Nominal stability). With terminal cost  $ Q_f $ the DARE solution at a nominal configuration  $ \kappa_0 $, if the QP is feasible at  $ k = 0 $ and the LPV variation  $ \|B_d(\kappa_k) - B_d(\kappa_0)\| $ is sufficiently small—quantified for this scalar plant in closed form as  $ \rho = \Lambda_{n,ref}/\Lambda_{n,true} < \rho^* \approx 3.4 $ (Proposition 1, derived in Appendix B), comfortably satisfied by the  $ 1.4\times $ workspace variation—the closed loop is asymptotically stable and  $ x_e(k) \to 0 $ (no disturbance), provided recursive feasibility holds.

Theorem 3 (ISS / offset-free). If  $ \|d(t)\| \leq \bar{d} $, the augmented system is observable, and the input-centered QP (10) is feasible,  $ (x_e, \hat{d}) $ is input-to-state stable with an error bound that scales with the unmodeled time variation of  $ d $. For constant matched disturbances in the nominal, free-space limit,  $ \hat{d} \to d_\infty $ implies  $ U_d = 1_N \Lambda_n d_\infty $ and  $ \Delta(d_\infty) + \Gamma U_d = 0 $, hence the unconstrained law becomes  $ F_{mpc} = \Lambda_n d_\infty + K_{eff} e + D_{eff} \dot{e} $ and the steady error is exactly zero. For slowly varying disturbances the residual error scales with  $ \|\dot{d}\| $. Under stiff contact the achievable steady-state error is additionally bounded by the force constraint and is therefore nonzero (Section VI-B confirms a contact-limited residual).

Proof status. Theorem 1 is supported by the sketch above. Theorems 2–3 follow standard arguments—terminal-cost/recursive-feasibility stability for constrained MPC [7] and the augmented-observer offset-free result [9]—specialized to the constant- $ A_d $ scalar plant with the input-centering identity  $ \Delta(\hat{d}) + \Gamma U_d(\hat{d}) = 0 $.

Proposition 1 (LPV stability margin). For the scalar plant (8), let  $ K = [k_1, k_2] $ be a gain designed at  $ \Lambda_{n,ref} $ (normalized to  $ \Lambda_{n,ref} = 1 $) and applied where the true inertia is  $ \Lambda_{n,true} $, giving the closed loop  $ A_{cl}(\rho) = A_d - \rho B_d (\Lambda_{n,ref}) K $ with  $ \rho = \Lambda_{n,ref} / \Lambda_{n,true} $ (since  $ B_d \propto \Lambda_n^{-1} $). Then  $ A_{cl}(\rho) $ is Schur for all  $ \rho \in (0, \rho^*) $ with

$$ \begin{align*}\rho^{\star}&=\min\Biggl\{\frac{2}{\Delta t\left|k_{2}\right|},\frac{2}{\Delta t\left|k_{2}-\frac{1}{2}\Delta t k_{1}\right|}\Biggr\}\\&=\frac{2}{\Delta t\left|k_{2}\right|},\end{align*} $$
